title: Ring operations for the maximal ind-etale subalgebra over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. For any commutative unital $k$-algebra $R$, including $R=0$, let $B_k(R)\subseteq R$ be the union of its finite etale unital $k$-subalgebras, as in [lem-sfb-finite-etale-subalgebra-directed-union]. Then $B_k(R)$ is reduced, meaning it has no nonzero nilpotent elements. Every unital $k$-algebra homomorphism $f:R\to S$ restricts to $B_k(R)\to B_k(S)$. If $R\subseteq S$ is a unital $k$-subalgebra, then $B_k(R)=R\cap B_k(S)$ inside $S$. Writing $R_{\mathrm{red}}=R/N_R$, where $N_R=\{r\in R:\exists n\geq1,\ r^n=0\}$ is the nilradical, the quotient map induces an isomorphism $B_k(R)\xrightarrow{\sim}B_k(R_{\mathrm{red}})$. For every finite family of commutative unital $k$-algebras $(R_i)_{i\in I}$, the projections identify $B_k(\prod_{i\in I}R_i)$ with $\prod_{i\in I}B_k(R_i)$, including the empty product, which is the zero ring. If $R\ne0$ and its only idempotents (elements satisfying $e^2=e$) are $0$ and $1$, then $B_k(R)$ is a field and is a separable algebraic extension of $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension].

source.place: Tag 0CKT, label lemma-properties-of-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra, parts (1), (2), (4), (5), (6); Tag 0CKR, label lemma-class-weakly-etale-over-field, parts (1), (3), identifies the finite-subalgebra union and gives reducedness. In part (6) explicitly require R nonzero; the zero algebra is otherwise a counterexample.

proof.text: For $x\in B_k(R)$ with $x^n=0$, choose a finite etale subalgebra $D\subseteq R$ containing $x$, using the union description. By the etale-over-a-field classification, $D$ is a finite product of finite separable fields. Each coordinate of $x$ has zero $n$th power in a field and hence is zero. Thus $x=0$. The empty product is already the zero ring, so this also covers $R=0$.

source.place: Tag 0CKR (1), (3), label lemma-class-weakly-etale-over-field; Tag 00U3, label lemma-etale-over-field

proof.text: Let $f:R\to S$ be a unital $k$-algebra map. For $x\in B_k(R)$ choose a finite etale subalgebra $D\subseteq R$ containing it. The image clause of the directed-union lemma applied to $f|_D$ says that $f(D)$ is a finite etale subalgebra of $S$. Hence $f(x)\in B_k(S)$. Corestriction of $f$ gives the required algebra map.

Assume $R\subseteq S$. Step 2 applied to the inclusion gives $B_k(R)\subseteq R\cap B_k(S)$. Conversely take $x\in R\cap B_k(S)$, and choose a finite etale $D\subseteq S$ containing $x$. The etale comparison theorem, clauses (1) and (4), makes $D/k$ weakly etale as a ring algebra. The weakly-etale-field lemma applied to the singly generated subalgebra $k[x]\subseteq D$ says that $k[x]$ is finite etale. The subalgebra $k[x]$ is contained in $R$ because $x\in R$ and the structural $k$-maps agree. Thus $x\in B_k(R)$ by the union description, proving equality.

source.place: Tag 0CKT (2) and Tag 0CKR (3), (5), labels lemma-properties-of-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra and lemma-class-weakly-etale-over-field

proof.text: Write $q:R\to R/N_R$. Step 2 gives $\bar q:B_k(R)\to B_k(R/N_R)$. If $x\in\ker\bar q$, then $x\in N_R$, so $x$ is nilpotent; Step 1 gives $x=0$. For surjectivity take $y\in B_k(R/N_R)$ in a finite etale subalgebra $D$ of $R/N_R$. Apply the etale nil-ideal lifting lemma to the base $A=k$, source algebra $C=D$, target algebra $T=R$, ideal $J=N_R$, and $g:D\hookrightarrow R/N_R$. Every element of $N_R$ is nilpotent by its definition, even when no power of this ideal vanishes. Obtain $h:D\to R$ with $qh=g$. The image clause of the directed-union lemma places $h(D)$ in $B_k(R)$, and $y=qh(y)$ is in the image of $\bar q$. This proves the claimed algebra isomorphism, in the quotient-induced direction.

source.place: Tag 0CKT (4), label lemma-properties-of-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra, with Tag 07K4, label lemma-smooth-strong-lift; correct the reversed arrows in the printed proof

proof.text: Put $P=\prod_{i\in I}R_i$. Step 2 for each projection gives $B_k(P)\subseteq\prod_i B_k(R_i)$. Conversely let $(x_i)\in\prod_i B_k(R_i)$, and for each of the finitely many indices choose a finite etale subalgebra $D_i\subseteq R_i$ containing $x_i$. Then $D=\prod_iD_i\subseteq P$ is a unital $k$-subalgebra and is etale by the finite-product lemma. It is finite over $k$: take finite $k$-module generating sets in the $D_i$ and insert each generator in its coordinate with zeros elsewhere; this finite set generates $D$. The definition of a finite affine morphism therefore makes $D$ finite etale. It contains $(x_i)$, proving the reverse inclusion. If $I$ is empty, both $P$ and its core are the zero ring; the same product lemma includes this case. The maps are exactly the restrictions of the projections, so this is the asserted identification of algebras.

source.place: Tag 0CKT (5), label lemma-properties-of-max-weakly-etale-subalgebra (proof omitted there); explicit finite-subalgebra argument using Tag 00U2 (11), label lemma-etale

proof.text: Finally suppose $R\ne0$ and $R$ has only idempotents $0,1$. For any $x\in B_k(R)$ choose finite etale $D\subseteq R$ containing $x$ and classify $D\cong\prod_{j\in F}L_j$. This product is nonzero because the subalgebra is unital in nonzero $R$, so $F$ is nonempty. If $F$ had two or more indices, a coordinate idempotent would be different from $0$ and $1$ in $D$, hence in $R$, a contradiction. Thus $D$ is a single finite separable field extension of $k$. For every nonzero $x$, its inverse in this $D$ belongs to $B_k(R)$; hence the nonzero ring $B_k(R)$ is a field. Every element lies in one of these finite separable fields. A polynomial over $k$ vanishes on $x$ in that field if and only if it vanishes in $B_k(R)$, since the inclusion is injective. Thus the monic minimal polynomial is the same, and is separable. This proves that $B_k(R)/k$ is separable algebraic.

lean.statement: theorem finiteEtaleSubalgebra_ring_operations (k : Type u) (R : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] : IsReduced (finiteEtaleSubalgebraUnion k R) ∧ (∀ (S : Type w) [CommRing S] [Algebra k S] (f : R →ₐ[k] S), ∃ g : finiteEtaleSubalgebraUnion k R →ₐ[k] finiteEtaleSubalgebraUnion k S, (finiteEtaleSubalgebraUnion k S).val.comp g = f.comp (finiteEtaleSubalgebraUnion k R).val) ∧ (∀ D : Subalgebra k R, (finiteEtaleSubalgebraUnion k D).map D.val = D ⊓ finiteEtaleSubalgebraUnion k R) ∧ (∃ e : finiteEtaleSubalgebraUnion k R ≃ₐ[k] finiteEtaleSubalgebraUnion k (R ⧸ nilradical R), ∀ x : finiteEtaleSubalgebraUnion k R, (e x).val = Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ k (nilradical R) x.val) ∧ (∀ (I : Type t) [Finite I] (A : I → Type w) [∀ i, CommRing (A i)] [∀ i, Algebra k (A i)], ∃ e : finiteEtaleSubalgebraUnion k (Π i, A i) ≃ₐ[k] (Π i, finiteEtaleSubalgebraUnion k (A i)), ∀ (x : finiteEtaleSubalgebraUnion k (Π i, A i)) (i : I), (e x i).val = x.val i) ∧ (Nontrivial R → (∀ e : R, e ^ 2 = e → e = 0 ∨ e = 1) → IsField (finiteEtaleSubalgebraUnion k R) ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable k (finiteEtaleSubalgebraUnion k R))
